newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks hit four-month high on reform pledge.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks hit four-month high on reform pledge.

text.p: Jordanian stocks rose to four-month highs on Tuesday as optimism over goverment commitment to economic reform pushed blue-chip shares upwards, brokers said.

The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index climbed 0.72 percent to 147.36 points, its highest level since May, in a healthy turnover of 527,018 shares worth 1.66 million dinars ($2.34 million).

"The market is stable. A little bit of confidence is back," broker Nasser al-Amad said. Investor sentiment was briefly shaken last month by unrest which hit southern Jordan after the government lifted bread subsidies.

He said traders were still fretting over high interest rates and a lack of cash liquidity which hampered investment in the market. Worries over tension in Jordan's neighbours, Israel and Iraq, also persisted.
"But people feel the government will take action to activate the economy now," Amad added.
Arab Bank led the rise in blue-chip shares and once again was the busiest stock, gaining 0.75 dinars to 240.50 after shares worth nearly 500,000 dinars changed hands.
Arab Potash also rose 0.07 dinars to 5.52 after shares worth 160,000 dinars were traded.
Volume was boosted on Tuesday by the return of Arab International for Investment and Education after its two-month suspension.
Shares worth 450,000 dinars were traded in the company, one of two private universities listed on the stock exchange, and the stock rose 0.16 dinars to close at 3.37.
"It's a good company with good profits, so people were waiting to get back into it," said a broker.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- rose 0.40 percent to 81.53 points, still 14.63 percent down on last year.
